title: Suggestions
intro: Improvements to the site and to the decision-making process, written so a reviewer can pick a path rather than inherit one. Each suggestion states the problem, the options with their cost and what they unlock, and a recommendation. Nothing here has been implemented. Item SG29 was added on 2026-11-14 (UTC) by the integration session (COORDINATION section 35) from the audit's promotion request R-A6.

items.title: Add a results backfill covering the whole season
items.problem: The out-of-sample window is 28 games because only 2026-11-08 onward was captured. The season began 2026-10-20, so roughly 200 games are missing and no strategy can reach the 30-play sample gate.

options.option: Backfill job that walks nba.com/games one date at a time from 2026-10-20
options.risk: Low - additive, existing files untouched
options.unlocks: Q2, F8, F9; every gate result becomes meaningful

options.option: Leave the window at 28 games and let it grow naturally
options.risk: High - roughly two more months before any strategy clears the sample gate
options.unlocks: Nothing new

items.recommendation: Take option 1. It is the cheapest change on this list and it is a prerequisite for four other items.
items.decision_needed: Approve the backfill run and confirm the retention policy for historical snapshots.

items.title: Log real closing prices
items.problem: Every 'edge' on the site is edge against a naive model standing in for the market (F3). Without real prices there is no way to say whether any of this is profitable.

options.option: Add data/raw/market.json populated from a licensed odds source, with a source field per row
options.risk: Medium - introduces a non-NBA source, so the per-row source link becomes mandatory
options.unlocks: Q1, Q8; real ROI; closing-line-value tracking

options.option: Manual closing-line log in a CSV committed to the repo
options.effort: Low per day, high over a season
options.risk: Medium - human transcription error
options.unlocks: The same thing, more slowly

options.option: Do nothing and keep the model-versus-reference framing
options.risk: High - the leaderboard can never claim profitability
options.unlocks: Nothing

items.recommendation: Option 1 if a licensed feed is available, option 2 as a stopgap. Until either happens, the site should keep saying 'model-vs-reference units' rather than 'profit'.
items.decision_needed: Whether to introduce a non-NBA data source at all, and which one.

items.title: Complete the player-minutes table
items.problem: Minutes are known for 50 of 465 players (F2). The availability impact is therefore a floor and is 0.00 for several teams that are clearly missing rotation players.

options.option: Fetch the official players table filtered by team, 30 requests, and union the results
options.risk: Low - same official source
options.unlocks: Q4, a trustworthy availability column, grading S6

options.option: Derive minutes from official box scores as they are captured
options.risk: Low
options.unlocks: Q3 and Q4 together

options.option: Keep the top-50 floor and publish the coverage column
options.risk: Medium - a 0.00 can be misread as 'no impact'
options.unlocks: Nothing

items.recommendation: Option 1 or 2. If neither is taken, the Injuries page must keep the coverage column and confidence label visible so a 0.00 is never read as healthy.
items.decision_needed: Which capture path to fund.

items.title: Show the confidence label next to every derived number
items.problem: The site mixes three kinds of number - official values, arithmetic on official values, and modelling choices. They look identical in a table.

options.option: Three-colour provenance chip on every cell: official, derived, assumption
options.risk: Low
options.unlocks: Trust; fewer misread tables

options.option: Keep provenance in a footnote column
options.risk: Medium - easy to miss
options.unlocks: Partial

items.recommendation: Option 1. The whole verification rule depends on the reader being able to tell these apart at a glance.
items.decision_needed: Visual treatment and whether the chip applies to every table or only the derived ones.

items.title: Add a graded-results page that updates itself
items.problem: Picks are published as PENDING and nothing currently grades them once games finish.

options.option: Extend the refresh job to re-grade every pending pick against the official final score and recompute the leaderboard
options.risk: Low
options.unlocks: A living leaderboard; the reward tiers start to mean something

options.option: Grade manually at the end of each week
options.risk: High - drift between what was published and what was graded
options.unlocks: Partial

items.recommendation: Option 1, and it should be automatic - grading must not depend on anyone remembering.
items.decision_needed: Whether graded picks overwrite the published slate or are kept alongside it.

items.title: Separate the two meanings of 'edge' everywhere in the UI
items.problem: 'Edge' currently means the gap between the originated number and the reference line. A reader will assume it means edge against a book.

options.option: Rename to 'model gap vs reference' throughout, with a tooltip
options.risk: Low
options.unlocks: Honesty at no cost

options.option: Keep 'edge' and add a banner
options.risk: Medium - banners get ignored
options.unlocks: Partial

items.recommendation: Option 1, and reserve the word 'edge' for a market comparison once SG2 lands.
items.decision_needed: Wording only.

items.title: Make the gates do something
items.problem: Gates are currently reported but not enforced: a strategy that fails G1 still appears on the Picks page.

options.option: Tier-driven staking - the leaderboard tier sets the published unit size, and anything below Tier 3 is published as paper only
options.risk: Low
options.unlocks: The leaderboard becomes an actual allocation rule

options.option: Hard suppression - hide plays from strategies that fail a gate
options.risk: Medium - hides information the reader may want
options.unlocks: Cleaner pick lists, less transparency

options.option: Report only
options.risk: Medium - invites reading research plays as recommendations
options.unlocks: Nothing

items.recommendation: Option 1. Tier-driven staking keeps the information visible while making the status unambiguous.
items.decision_needed: Unit sizes per tier, and whether paper-only plays are visually separated.

items.title: Handle overtime and extreme games explicitly
items.problem: A 284-point double-overtime game sits in a 28-game sample and inflates the fitted total-error spread, which in turn flattens every probability the model produces.

options.option: Model regulation separately and add an overtime term
options.risk: Medium
options.unlocks: Q7, better total calibration

options.option: Winsorise the residuals when fitting the spread
options.risk: Medium - hides genuine tail risk
options.unlocks: More stable parameters now

options.option: Leave it and grow the sample
options.risk: Medium
options.unlocks: Nothing

items.recommendation: Option 2 as a stopgap alongside SG1; revisit option 1 once the sample is large enough to evaluate it.
items.decision_needed: Whether tail risk should be damped or modelled.

items.title: Add an Emirates NBA Cup adjustment - but only after measuring it
items.problem: The 2026-11-13 slate is entirely Cup group play. Point differential is the Cup tiebreaker, which could change late-game behaviour, but nothing in the data measures it (Q6).

options.option: Measure first with the backfilled results, then add a term only if the effect is real
options.risk: Low
options.unlocks: Q6

options.option: Add a speculative Cup term now
options.risk: High - this is exactly the kind of unfounded adjustment the project is supposed to avoid
options.unlocks: Nothing reliable

items.recommendation: Option 1. Do not add it until it is measured.
items.decision_needed: Whether to fund the measurement.

items.title: Publish the daily refresh log on the site
items.problem: The refresh job has never run (F7), and if it fails silently the site will quietly go stale while still looking current.

options.option: Write a run record each time (timestamp, rows changed, any failure) and show it on the Sources page
options.risk: Low
options.unlocks: Visible freshness; F7 closes itself

options.option: Rely on the Actions log in GitHub
options.risk: Medium - not visible to a site visitor
options.unlocks: Partial

items.recommendation: Option 1. A stale data set presented as current is the worst failure mode this site has.
items.decision_needed: Where the run record lives and how long it is retained.

items.title: Make the horizon the centre of the site, not a page inside it
items.problem: The repository had grown two complete sites plus three sets of pages, and the landing page led with a research narrative rather than with the next three days of games. A decision-maker opening the site had to find the picks page before finding out what was on tonight.

options.option: Single generated site: one landing page that states the horizon, the status and the open flags, with one page per category and every row source-linked
options.effort: Medium - one generator, no build step at deploy time
options.risk: Low - additive; the two earlier builds stay online as archives
options.unlocks: SG12, SG13; the site becomes usable without knowing the repository's history

options.option: Keep the two parallel builds and add a third landing that only links to them
options.risk: High - three navigation models, three data models, and the reader still has to know which one to trust
options.unlocks: Nothing

items.recommendation: Option 1. It is what this build did. The earlier builds are preserved and linked as archives rather than deleted.
items.decision_needed: Confirm that the earlier builds stay reachable as archives, and decide whether the root landing page should keep any pointer to them at all.

items.title: Put the unverified column on every table instead of only on the flags page
items.problem: A reader who lands on the Picks page sees numbers. The fact that the ratings end at 11/12, that five of ten teams had not filed an injury report, and that no price feed exists is on a different page. That is a decision-making risk: a number that is a lower bound looks like a number that is a fact.

options.option: Render unconfirmed values as an em dash with a hover explanation, and print a coverage line under each table stating exactly what is missing
options.effort: Low - a single rendering rule in the generator
options.risk: None
options.unlocks: A reader can tell an unverified value from a measured one without leaving the page

options.option: Leave the flags page as the single place the gaps are recorded
options.risk: Medium to high - the flags page is the least-read page on the site
options.unlocks: Nothing

items.recommendation: Option 1, and it is already in place on this build: every table that cannot be sourced says so in the row itself.
items.decision_needed: Decide whether the hover text should be expanded into a visible column, which is friendlier on a phone and worse for scanning on a wide screen.

items.title: Add a one-screen answer to 'what should I look at tonight'
items.problem: The site publishes 27 games and 63 paper picks. Nothing ranks them, because ranking on a model edge that has not cleared the skill gate would be misleading. The reader is left to do the sorting themselves.

options.option: Rank by the gates, not by the edge: surface the games whose edge survives the availability and stability checks, and show the gate status next to each one
options.risk: Medium - any ranking risks being read as a recommendation, so it must carry the gate status inline
options.unlocks: A shortlist that is defensible; SG14

options.option: Publish an even slate with no ranking at all
options.risk: Low
options.unlocks: Nothing - it is what the site does today

items.recommendation: Option 1, but only once the price feed in SG2 exists. Before then any ranking is a ranking of model noise, and a shortlist that looks like a recommendation is the most dangerous thing this site could publish.
items.decision_needed: Confirm the ordering rule, and confirm that no ranking appears until a strategy has cleared G4.

items.title: Make the verification reproducible by anyone, not only by this repository
items.problem: Every number on the site is meant to be checkable against an official page, and each row carries its link. But a reviewer who wants to confirm the build itself has to read five Python scripts and know which raw file feeds which output.

options.option: Publish a one-page provenance map: raw snapshot, the script that consumed it, the output file and the page it reached, with a link to each
options.effort: Low - the mapping already exists in the code
options.risk: None
options.unlocks: Independent verification; SG15

options.option: Leave provenance in the repository and in COORDINATION.md
options.risk: Medium - a reviewer has to reconstruct it
options.unlocks: Nothing

items.recommendation: Option 1. The mapping is already in the code; it needs a page.
items.decision_needed: Confirm the level of detail: one line per output file, or one line per individual table row.

items.title: Publish one line set, one ratings window, one sign convention
items.problem: Two projection sets with different ratings windows are published together, and they disagree on every game with a Build B point-spread pick (F26). Their 'spread (home)' fields use opposite sign conventions under similar labels (F27).

options.option: Keep the Build D horizon (ratings through games of 11/12), regenerate the landing page and picks from it, and retire the Build B horizon lines
options.effort: Medium - one builder change and a regenerated site
options.risk: Medium - Build B's 63 rows must be re-derived; the settled 11/13 record is unaffected
options.unlocks: One set of lines for every page; Source Check section 5 becomes empty

options.option: Keep Build B (ratings through 11/05) and state its window everywhere
options.risk: High - the ratings are a week older than the latest official games
options.unlocks: A stable reference, but a known-stale one

options.option: Keep both, label each by its ratings window, and never put them in one table
options.risk: Medium - two numbers for one game remain on the site
options.unlocks: Transparency without a decision

items.recommendation: Option 1. The newer ratings use every official game through 11/12. Adopt the sign convention of Build A (home spread = minus the projected home margin) on every page.
items.decision_needed: Reviewer: which line set is the published horizon. No pick should be published until this is decided.

items.title: Make the official-value check part of the gate
items.problem: VERIFY OK checks that links resolve and rows have sources, not that values match NBA.com (F34). The conflicts in F26, F27 and F29 passed it.

options.option: Run scripts/source_check.py inside scripts/verify_all.py and fail on any horizon or finished-game mismatch that is not listed in the flagged register
options.effort: Low - the checker exists and reads committed files
options.risk: Low - the failure is visible and the register is the escape hatch
options.unlocks: A gate that tests values, not only structure

options.option: Keep the structural gate and review values by hand before each publish
options.effort: None now; a manual step later
options.risk: High - manual review is what missed these items
options.unlocks: Nothing new

items.recommendation: Option 1. The check takes seconds, and it is the only check on this list that would have caught the conflicts before publication.
items.decision_needed: Reviewer: approve adding the checker to the gate.

items.title: Finish the game-log capture so props stop being a point estimate with no width
items.problem: Ten players now have measured dispersion; 78 horizon prop rows still publish no probability (Q3, F40, F42). The projection and the anchor differ by at most 0.52 of a measured SD, so nothing is settable - and that verdict rests on three or four games a player.

options.option: Capture the full horizon: every player on every prop row, each morning of the slate, into data/proplogs/<date>/, and let scripts/prop_variance.py price all of them
options.effort: Medium - one page read per player, 50 players a day; the parser and the gates already exist
options.risk: Low - a failed read leaves the row blank, as it is now
options.unlocks: A probability column on every prop row, a settable/unsettable split per slate, and a grading history from the next day onward

options.option: Go deep instead of wide: a season-long game log for one fixed cohort of 15-20 parlay-eligible players, refreshed weekly
options.effort: High once, low after - the first pull is 40+ games a player
options.risk: Medium - the cohort ages out of the slate
options.unlocks: The one thing a Last-5 window cannot give: a measurable prop-prop correlation (F42) and a usable parlay rho instead of a declared one

options.option: Stop originating props until either of the above exists
options.risk: Low - the page already publishes no funded prop
options.unlocks: Nothing, and it removes the only place the desk learns what a prop needs

items.recommendation: Option 1 first, then option 2 for the parlay cohort. Option 1 is what turns 78 blank cells into numbers with sources; option 2 is the only route to a measured rho, and it is worth doing after the desk has a week of graded props to judge.
items.decision_needed: Reviewer: pick 1, 2 or 1+2 in that order. Nothing on the site changes until the capture runs, because the script already reads whatever is in data/proplogs/.

items.title: Replace the flat 0.55 production-transfer rule with per-stat minutes elasticities
items.problem: scripts/injury_impact.py and originate_horizon.py move a line by a declared constant (production_transfer = 0.55) for any absent player, whatever the stat. Measured on 40 official box scores, points move at about 1.29x their minutes share and assists at 0.49x - one flat number is wrong in both directions (A15).

options.option: Fit per-stat betas (points, rebounds, assists, PRA) on the season-long logs once SG17 option 2 exists, and let the injury module use the stat-specific figure
options.effort: Medium - the regression is 20 lines of the existing script
options.risk: Low - the declared constant stays as the fallback where a beta is not yet fitted
options.unlocks: An injury adjustment with a measured coefficient instead of an asserted one, which is what gate G7 needs to stop being un-runnable

options.option: Keep 0.55 and publish this measurement beside it as a caveat
options.risk: Medium - the number keeps moving lines while being known to be flat
options.unlocks: Nothing

options.option: Re-fit now on the 40 captured rows
options.risk: High - n=40 from 10 players over one week, and the page itself says so (F44); a line moved on it is moved on noise
options.unlocks: A demonstration, not a decision

items.recommendation: Option 1, sequenced behind SG17 option 2. Do not re-fit on this week's sample to move a live line.
items.decision_needed: Reviewer: approve the per-stat direction now (so the module's declared assumption is on the record as unmeasured) and schedule the fit for when the sample exists.

items.title: Cut the pickable horizon against the game-day edition, and freeze at that cut
items.problem: The pipeline currently originates and publishes lines against whatever edition the overnight capture found. For a 7:00 PM ET slate that is up to fifteen hours before the league's own game-day window closes, and the measured consequence is on the site: four clubs filed in the meantime and the model line for their games moved by 0.0 to 2.6 points only because the rest of the names could not be priced at all.

options.option: Add a 15:15 UTC scheduled capture immediately before the first 7:00 PM ET tip, and let that cut be the published line set for the day
options.effort: Low - the refresh workflow already runs at 15:15 UTC; the change is which edition it treats as final
options.risk: Low - additive; earlier lines stay archived and graded, they are not rewritten
options.unlocks: Q10, Q14 (now answered), Q18 (now answered); every pick then reflects what a person watching the report at 3 p.m. ET could see

options.option: Keep the overnight cut as the official line set and publish only the game-day delta, as the Game-Day Read page does now
options.effort: None - this is the current behaviour
options.risk: Low, but the published number is knowingly stale by one filing window
options.unlocks: Nothing new; it preserves pre-registration purity at the cost of usefulness

options.option: Re-price the published lines in place when a newer edition arrives
options.risk: Fatal for the leaderboard - it puts information published after the cut inside a line that will later be graded, which is the look-ahead error this repository has already been burned by
options.unlocks: Nothing; rejected and recorded so nobody re-proposes it

items.recommendation: Option A, with the frozen copy kept and diffed. Publish a line, then a delta, never a mutated line.
items.decision_needed: Which edition is the day's official cut, and what time the scheduler should fire.

items.title: Either give every listed player a minutes row or stop printing 0.00 for an unknown
items.problem: The availability impact is computed as (status weight x minutes share) x 15.0, and a player with no minutes row contributes 0.00 - indistinguishable in the table from a player whose absence costs nothing. Tonight that is 20 of the 24 rows the game-day edition added and 45 of the 50 rows it lists for the five games - it is the difference between a line that moved and a line that did not.

options.option: Capture minutes per club from the official team pages (30 URLs) instead of the paginated top-50 league table
options.effort: Medium - one fetch per club plus a parser; no new permission or vendor needed
options.risk: Low - additive; the existing table stays as the cross-check
options.unlocks: Q12, Q3, Q20 and F47; prop projections stop being a point estimate with no width

options.option: Render a dash, not 0.00, wherever minutes are unknown, and exclude the row from the team total with the exclusion counted in the header
options.effort: Low - one formatting rule and one counter
options.risk: Low, but it makes published impacts smaller-looking because fewer players count at all
options.unlocks: Removes a misleading zero from every table today, including this one

options.option: Do nothing and keep the lower-bound note
options.risk: Medium - the note is correct and unread; readers keep seeing 0.00 as 'healthy'
options.unlocks: Nothing

items.recommendation: Both of the first two: the dash is a one-line honesty fix that should ship now, the per-club capture is the actual repair.
items.decision_needed: Whether the reviewer wants a data project (option A) or a display fix (option B) this week.

items.title: Show an edition timeline per game: what the model knew, and when
items.problem: Every table on the site carries a source id, so a reader can find WHERE a value came from, but nothing shows WHEN a row ceased to be the newest word. Today the gap between the edition behind the lines and the newest published edition was nine hours and seventeen minutes, and it could only be discovered by opening two PDFs.

options.option: A per-game timeline strip on the Game-Day Read page: each edition, its timestamp, the number of rows it added or changed, and whether the site's line was cut before or after it
options.effort: Low - the data already exists in data/derived/gameday_read.json
options.risk: Low
options.unlocks: Makes staleness visible at a glance, which is the single decision-support gap this session found

options.option: A single 'age of newest edition' badge in the header of every page
options.risk: Low
options.unlocks: Coarser, but it is impossible to miss

items.recommendation: Option A first; the badge follows for free.
items.decision_needed: None technically - a reviewer only has to say whether per-game or global.

items.title: Never display a season leader without the report's verdict on him
items.problem: The official game cards print a season leader for each club that is a pure season-average read-out. On 2026-11-16 that widget shows Anthony Edwards for Minnesota while the report rules him out, and on 11/14 it shows Caleb Wilson for Chicago, also out (F49). Any prop table or card copy that inherits that name is quoting a player who is not playing.

options.option: Join the leader line to the current report at render time and mark a ruled-out leader in place, keeping the published value visible next to the mark
options.effort: Low - the join key already exists in the capture
options.risk: Low
options.unlocks: Removes the most likely way a confident-looking wrong name gets onto a pick slip

options.option: Drop the leader widget from the capture entirely and derive leaders from the players table only
options.risk: Low
options.unlocks: One fewer source of unprefixed third-party-looking numbers, at the cost of context

items.recommendation: Option A. The card is official and should stay cited; it should stop being unqualified.
items.decision_needed: Whether a marked leader may still be shown as the leader.

items.title: Do not let a follow-up commit cancel the deploy it is describing
items.problem: The Pages workflow now isolates PR runs from production runs (PR #75), but production still cancels in progress. A seat that merges a change and then pushes a board-record commit within a minute cancels its own deploy and leaves a `cancelled` badge on the merge commit. Two seats have now reported a Pages deploy as 'confirmed' off a run id, and a cancelled run is not a deploy.

options.option: `cancel-in-progress: false` on the production group only, keeping the PR behaviour as is
options.risk: Low - a queued production run waits instead of being replaced; the queue already serialises them
options.unlocks: Every deploy claim in COORDINATION.md points at a run that actually finished

options.option: Commit convention: fold the delivery record into the merge commit, so main sees one push per change
options.effort: Zero code, but it constrains how seats write the board
options.risk: Low
options.unlocks: Also removes most of the COORDINATION.md collision churn that forced four renumberings

items.recommendation: Option A, because it makes the badge truthful rather than asking every session to remember a convention. Option B costs nothing and can be adopted today.
items.decision_needed: Whether the project wants a superseded production deploy to be cancelled (cheap) or to finish (auditable).

items.title: Classify every table row without an NBA link as fact, derived or repository-internal
items.problem: 207 of 5,940 HTML table rows carry no official NBA link (F66). Some state NBA facts, some are methodology or repository-internal rows where no NBA source applies. The blanket rule cannot be satisfied honestly without a classification.

options.option: (a) rows that state an NBA fact must link nba.com/official.nba.com
options.effort: one classification pass over the register
options.risk: low - nothing is deleted
options.unlocks: an honest strict count that can only go to zero for real

options.option: (b) rows derived from linked inputs carry a visible 'derived - inputs linked' mark
options.risk: low
options.unlocks: derived numbers stop looking like captured facts

options.option: (c) repository-internal rows carry a visible non-NBA label
options.risk: low
options.unlocks: methodology rows can never masquerade as verified NBA facts

items.decision_needed: Reviewer, row by row on the Flagged register - no count may be closed by inference.
items.recommendation: Adopt (a)+(b)+(c) as the written policy, then work the register in one pass; the strict counts stay published until then.

items.title: Calibrate a per-game overtime probability instead of a flat measured rate
items.problem: After F53 the P(OT) column prices the measured season rate (0.0500, 8/160) for every game. That is honest but coarse: a projected one-possession game and a projected 15-point spread show the same number.

options.option: (a) scale the margin-density approximation so its season mean matches the measured rate
options.effort: one fitted multiplier plus a disclosure
options.risk: medium - a fudge factor on a thin sample
options.unlocks: per-game P(OT) differentiation today

options.option: (b) wait for 200+ games and fit a logistic on |expected margin|
options.risk: low
options.unlocks: a defensible per-game estimator

options.option: (c) capture play-by-play and model overtime directly
options.risk: blocked by Q5
options.unlocks: real game-flow metrics

items.decision_needed: Model owner, when the sample supports it.
items.recommendation: (a) as an interim, published next to the measured rate with both labelled; (b) as the real fix. Until then the flat rate is the honest price.

items.title: Split rest_days into gap_days and days_off in the shared builders (R-29-3)
items.problem: One field name carries two definitions: engine/validate.py counts calendar gap (back-to-back = 1), scripts/originate_horizon.py counts full days off (back-to-back = 0). Two published pages therefore disagree about the same team-night. Both definitions are correct; the shared name is the defect (F-S29-04).

options.option: (a) publish both columns with distinct names (gap_days, days_off) and keep b2b as a derived flag
options.effort: builder field rename plus page relabels
options.risk: low - no value changes
options.unlocks: both conventions readable; the same team-night can never disagree with itself

options.option: (b) standardise on one definition and relabel the other page
options.risk: medium - one page silently changes meaning
options.unlocks: a single number per team-night

items.decision_needed: Integration seat + engine owners; affects both builders' outputs.
items.recommendation: (a): nothing is lost, nothing is silently reinterpreted, and readers can see both conventions.

items.title: Get a dated, licensed closing-price source - or write down that the site stays price-free (R-29-7)
items.problem: No NBA-operated source publishes a sportsbook price, so the market-edge gate (GG) cannot run and no strategy anywhere in the repository can be called a market edge (I-30-3, F3). 'Edge' remains model-vs-naive-reference.

options.option: (a) license a dated closing-price feed and log prices at tip
options.risk: licensing terms
options.unlocks: the market-edge gate (GG) can run; strategies can be called market edges

options.option: (b) declare the site permanently price-free and drop market claims everywhere
options.risk: none
options.unlocks: honest scope forever; no gate GG by construction

options.option: (c) manual price logging by a human
options.risk: violates the no-manual-input rule unless someone owns it
options.unlocks: slow price history

items.decision_needed: Project owner (human) - this is a licensing and budget decision, not a modelling one.
items.recommendation: Decide explicitly; until then keep every edge claim scoped to model-vs-reference, as the site already does.

items.title: Stop the probe workflow from pushing record commits onto open session branches
items.problem: probe-official.yml commits its record to arena/** branches and main after each run, which made every open PR CONFLICTING today and churned Pages builds (F68). The pages.yml concurrency fix stopped runs cancelling each other; the record commits still dirty branches.

options.option: (a) probe commits carry [skip ci] and target main only
options.risk: low
options.unlocks: session branches stop getting dirty probe commits

options.option: (b) probe writes an Actions artifact; a scheduled job commits the record to main
options.risk: low
options.unlocks: the same, with cleaner separation

items.decision_needed: Workflow owner.
items.recommendation: (a) or (b); the probe record's job is to evidence reachability, not to ride every session branch.

items.title: Promote refreshed captures into published picks only through the gate suite, never by hand or silently
items.problem: The scheduled refresh captures official data into capture-only branches/PRs, but promotion into published picks is a separate manual step; a refresh can therefore sit unpromoted (stale site) or be promoted without the gates having run on it (unchecked site). Requested by the independent audit (COORDINATION R-A6).

options.option: A. A promotion workflow: merge a capture PR only when verify_all + check_site + verify_dashboard + render_check pass on the merged tree, then regenerate picks in the same run; otherwise keep the prior slate with an explicit stale marker.
options.effort: Medium - the gates already run in CI; wiring them to the capture PR is mostly configuration
options.risk: Low - gates can only block, never invent
options.unlocks: Refreshed data reaches the site on a measured path; staleness becomes visible instead of silent

options.option: B. Manual promotion with a required checklist recorded in COORDINATION.md.
options.risk: Medium - depends on a human remembering; today's staleness flags came from exactly that
options.unlocks: Nothing new

items.decision_needed: A or B, and who signs the promotion record.
items.recommendation: A.

items.title: Adopt the rolling-slate cadence as the standing daily process
items.problem: The 2026-11-15 session had to hand-run capture, settlement, ledger, horizon roll and rebuild. The brief requires a scheduled job with freshness + provenance gates before rebuild; manual runs do not scale and skip gates silently.

options.option: A: refresh-data.yml cron captures everything, runs the full pipeline (capture -> verify -> settle -> roll -> rebuild -> gate) and opens a PR with the gate report attached (auto-merge only when all gates pass)
options.effort: Medium - extend the workflow and gate script (drafted in this PR)
options.risk: Low - capture-only commits remain; promotion stays a PR with the gate report
options.unlocks: The brief's scheduled-job requirement end to end; SG30 decision A

options.option: B: cron captures only (current design) and a human/session promotes snapshots by PR
options.risk: Medium - manual steps get skipped under load; no gate report travels with promotion
options.unlocks: Nothing new

options.option: C: cron captures + auto-commits to a data branch; a weekly session promotes
options.risk: Medium - weekly cadence is stale for a rolling slate
options.unlocks: Some automation

items.recommendation: A. The brief says no waiting for user review and no manual input; A keeps the promotion honest because the gate report travels with the PR and a failing gate blocks the merge.
items.decision_needed: Reviewer picks A, B or C before the workflow is extended (the engine additions for standings + teams/traditional + teams/opponent and the gate step are already drafted in this PR as the basis for A).

items.title: Close the OT-column reconciliation (F75) with a full per-game re-read
items.problem: Standings OT columns sum to 9 overtime games through 2026-11-14 while the verified finals show 8. One value is unreconciled and stays flagged.

options.option: A: re-read every game result page from 2026-10-21 (season start) to 2026-11-14 at the next refresh and rebuild the gamelog as the single OT source of truth
options.risk: Low - additive transcription with source links
options.unlocks: F75 close; full-season result feed the brief asks for

options.option: B: reconcile only the teams whose OT records imply an OT game not in the gamelog (narrower read)
options.effort: Low - a handful of team pages
options.risk: Low
options.unlocks: F75 close on the flagged value

options.option: C: leave the flag open and never use OT counts in any published metric
options.risk: Low but the brief's per-game result feed stays incomplete
options.unlocks: Nothing

items.recommendation: B first (cheap, targeted), then A inside the weekly full re-read that the refresh job already performs.
items.decision_needed: Confirm B (targeted) or A (full) so the next refresh allocates the fetch budget accordingly.

items.title: Capture per-player minutes for all 30 teams so the redistribution gate measures the model, not the capture
items.problem: Eleven of the twenty-five picks in the current window are held back by minutes capture, not by the model: seven fail the minutes-redistribution gate outright and four more carry a blank availability cell. The stored capture is the league-wide top 50 by minutes (page 1 of 10).

options.option: A: one official request per team (30 requests) for the per-game traditional player table, stored per team with its retrieval stamp
options.effort: Low - one loop over the 30 team ids
options.risk: Low - additive capture, additive file
options.unlocks: every pick becomes gateable on redistribution; the availability column fills in for CHI, MEM, SAS, CHA, MIL and the rest

options.option: B: find the working pagination parameter on the league leaders table and capture all 10 pages
options.effort: Medium - requires probing the rendered slice
options.risk: Medium - the parameter was already shown not to be honoured once
options.unlocks: the same coverage in one file, if the parameter can be found

options.option: C: leave it and publish the gate failure as the verdict
options.risk: High - the gate then reports a data gap as if it were a model result
options.unlocks: nothing

items.title: Make one official endpoint the source of truth for tip times and fail the refresh on a disagreement
items.problem: Two official captures disagreed on the tip time of GSW@NOP (09:00 PM ET vs 8:00 PM ET). Nothing in the pipeline detects that class of conflict today; the newest capture simply overwrites.

options.option: A: designate the per-date games page as the tip-time source, normalise the format, and record a conflict row whenever two captures of one game id differ
options.risk: Low
options.unlocks: F101 closes; tip-time provenance becomes auditable per game

options.option: B: cross-check tip time against the injury PDF's Game Time column as well
options.risk: Low
options.unlocks: a third official corroboration, but the PDF only covers games with a submitted report

items.recommended: A, then B as a cross-check

items.title: Read quarter scores from the official box score so the results feed matches the brief
items.problem: The brief asks for one row per game with date, teams, final score and quarter scores. The results feed carries date, teams and final; the quarter columns are null because the box score was not read in this pass.

options.option: A: after each slate completes, read the official box score for every game and store the four (or more) quarter lines, asserting that they sum to the printed final
options.effort: Medium - one box score per game per day
options.risk: Low
options.unlocks: the results feed matches the brief outright, and the assertion catches transcription errors

options.option: B: derive quarters from play-by-play
options.risk: Medium - more endpoints, more to get wrong
options.unlocks: the same data plus timing detail that is not needed for settlement

items.title: Refuse to promote a team-stat capture while any game on the previous slate is still in progress
items.problem: Cutting model inputs from an efficiency table during a live slate produces a table in which some teams include that slate's games and some do not. This session avoided it by using the last clean snapshot, but the pipeline would not have stopped anyone.

options.option: A: add a freshness gate to the refresh job - promote a team-stat capture only when every game on the most recent slate is final
options.risk: Low - the previous capture simply stays in force
options.unlocks: F103 closes; every published line is cut from a consistent game set

options.option: B: cut twice, once clean and once current, and publish the drift between them
options.risk: Low
options.unlocks: the same guarantee plus a visible measure of how much a slate moves the inputs

items.title: Re-read the injury index inside the refresh job so availability fills in game date by game date
items.problem: Availability is the one column that changes fastest and it is currently captured only when a session happens to look. No official edition covers 11/17 or 11/18 yet, so fifteen of twenty-five picks carry a blank cell.

options.option: A: have the scheduled refresh read the injury index, take the newest edition, diff it against the stored one, and re-cut the availability column only (leaving frozen pre-registration untouched)
options.risk: Low - additive to the existing refresh gate
options.unlocks: the 11/17 and 11/18 columns fill in as the league publishes; F105 closes

options.option: B: keep manual per-session capture
options.risk: High - the column is as stale as the last session that looked
options.unlocks: nothing

items.title: Give GitHub Pages one deploy path instead of two that race each other
items.problem: Pages is configured with build_type 'legacy' - it builds the site from the main branch itself - while .github/workflows/pages.yml also deploys an Actions artifact to the same environment. Two builders are writing one site. Measured at 2026-11-16T02:5xZ: 9 consecutive 'pages build and deployment' runs cancelled, one every few minutes, each cancelled by the next push to main, with the last successful build at 2026-11-15T23:44:35Z. Freeing the queue (SG23, PR #115) did not fix it because the starvation is structural, not a backlog.

options.option: A: switch Pages to the Actions build type, so pages.yml is the only deploy path
options.effort: Low - one API call or one setting in Settings > Pages
options.risk: Low - pages.yml already produces the artifact and its deploy job has a concurrency group that serialises production runs (cancel-in-progress false on main)
options.unlocks: F97 closes; the site stops depending on how many sessions happen to be pushing

options.option: B: delete pages.yml and let the legacy branch builder be the only path
options.risk: Medium - loses the validate gate that runs before deploy, so a broken page could publish
options.unlocks: the same single path, but without the pre-deploy check

options.option: C: leave both paths
options.risk: High - the site keeps serving whatever build happened to finish, which during parallel sessions is an old commit
options.unlocks: nothing

items.note: This session's token returned HTTP 403 on PUT /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pages (build_type=workflow), so it could not be applied here; it needs a repository admin.

items.title: Stop writing scores for games that have not been played
items.problem: The dated result captures write home_pts 0 / away_pts 0 with game_status 1 for every scheduled fixture, and the horizon generator keeps those rows in data/official/. Four model inputs read that corpus; each had to invent its own filter, and three of them got it wrong (F129): the published home-court block, the per-team luck z-scores and the measured correlations were all computed over 25 games that had not happened, and the margin dispersion that converts the home-win rate into points was diluted by 25 zero margins.

options.option: A: have the capture write null for a non-final game and assert it at promotion
options.effort: Low - one guard in engine/promote_official.py plus a schema check
options.risk: Low - consumers already treat None as not-a-game; a 0-0 game is not a legal final anyway
options.unlocks: every count-based number stops depending on each consumer remembering to filter

options.option: B: keep the payload and make the shared predicate the only definition
options.risk: Medium - the next consumer that filters on 'score is not None' reintroduces the bug
options.unlocks: nothing new; it preserves what this session fixed

options.option: C: both - write nulls and keep the predicate as a backstop
options.risk: Low
options.unlocks: the defect cannot come back quietly from either side

items.note: The predicate is already in place and tested; A is the remaining half. Until A lands, any new script that sums over data/official/results_*.json must import is_verified_final - worth a line in the README.

items.title: One provenance manifest for the archived injury PDFs
items.problem: 76 of 88 sidecars use {url, retrieved_utc, revision_label, http_status, ...}; the newest 12 use {edition, source_url, retrieved_at_utc, content_type}. Same facts, two spellings, so a consumer that reads one name sees blanks for the other (F130). Requirement R04 is satisfied only because the auditor checks both.

options.option: A: normalise the fetcher to one schema and rewrite the 12 older sidecars in a migration commit
options.effort: Low - 12 files, mechanical, byte hashes untouched
options.risk: Low - the PDF bytes and their sha256 are not modified, so tamper-evidence is unaffected
options.unlocks: the archive can be audited by one reader, and the diff chain can key off retrieval time alone

options.option: B: keep both and make the verifier accept either
options.risk: Medium - the ambiguity stays and every future consumer re-solves it
options.unlocks: nothing new

options.option: C: add the revision time printed inside the PDF to the sidecar as a separate field
options.effort: Medium - needs the PDF text parse engine/injury_diff.py already does
options.risk: Low
options.unlocks: R18's banner can show the league's own revision stamp, not just our retrieval time

items.note: Do not re-download anything to do A: the sidecar is metadata, the evidence is the stored bytes.

items.title: Gate the build on pin currency: fail when the published HCA pin is older than the newest standings capture
items.problem: The published pin sat at 102/193 = 0.5285 for 16 hours after the league's own standings had moved to 102/196 = 0.5204, and the capture that produced it carried a caveat saying three games were still in progress. Nothing failed. A session read the standings, wrote the number into the board, asked an integration seat to apply it, and the model kept shipping the stale one (R09, request R-50-B). The pin is only 'pinned to the measurement' if something checks that it still is.

options.option: A: a build-time assertion that the pin equals a re-derivation from the newest standings capture
options.effort: Low - scripts/test_hca_pin.py already re-derives it; promote it into the CI validate job
options.risk: Low - a stale pin then blocks a rebuild instead of shipping quietly
options.unlocks: this class of defect cannot reach the published site again

options.option: B: also fail when the standings capture itself is older than the newest settled game day
options.effort: Low - the comparison is a date string against data/settlement/
options.risk: Medium - a quiet night could block a rebuild for no good reason; state the tolerance
options.unlocks: a pin computed from an obviously stale read stops being publishable

options.option: C: publish the pin's age on every page that uses it
options.effort: Low - the capture already carries retrieved_utc
options.risk: None
options.unlocks: a reader can see the input is 3 hours old or 3 days old without opening a JSON file

items.note: Test A exists in this branch already (scripts/test_hca_pin.py) but is not wired into .github/workflows/pages.yml; wiring it is a one-line change in the validate job.

items.title: Print the two rho prices side by side everywhere, not only on the roll page
items.problem: After this session's fix the data files carry both numbers - naive product, rho-adjusted, fair American odds, the rho's n and interval - but only the rolling-slate page renders them. site/pages/parlay-pricing.html and the SGP candidates table still render one column each, so a reader comparing the two surfaces sees a price without its assumption on one of them.

options.option: A: one shared parlay table component used by both pages
options.effort: Medium - both builders must import it
options.risk: Low - the numbers are already in the JSON
options.unlocks: the naive-vs-correlated comparison becomes impossible to omit by accident

options.option: B: add the missing columns to the older page only
options.risk: Low - duplicates the markup, which is how the drift happened
options.unlocks: the same information, less safely

options.option: C: leave it; the roll page is the surface of record
options.risk: Medium - the brief's 'price every parlay and print the naive product beside it' is then satisfied on the data but not on every page
options.unlocks: nothing

items.note: The register rows carry rho_status strings long enough to print under the number; no new data is needed.
